{{short description|Croatian-French biologist}}
[[File:Miroslav Radman, 2019.jpg|thumb|Radman at the 2019 [[FEMS]] Summer School for Postdocs]]
'''Miroslav Radman''' (born April 30, 1944) is a [[Croatia]]n-[[France|French]] biologist.

==Biography==

Radman was born in [[Split (city)|Split]], [[PR Croatia]], [[Yugoslavia]]. From 1962–1967 he studied experimental biology, [[physical chemistry]] and [[molecular biology]] at the [[University of Zagreb]] and in 1969 he obtained a doctorate degree in [[molecular biology]] at the [[Free University of Brussels (1834–1969)|Free University of Brussels]].  He spent the next three years at [[Harvard University]] as a [[postdoctoral research]]er. From 1973 until 1983 he was Professor of Molecular Biology at the Free University of Brussels and from 1983 until 1998 the Research Director at the French Centre for Scientific Research at the University of Paris 7. He is now a professor of [[cellular biology]] at the Faculté de Médecine – Necker, Université Paris V, [[Paris, France]]. In  2002 he became a full member of the French Academy of Sciences, the first [[Croat]] to do so in the Academy's history. Radman is a co-founder of the Mediterranean Institute For Life Sciences located in [[Split, Croatia|Split]], [[Croatia]].<ref name="BioFR"/><ref name="BioEN"/>

==Scientific work==

Radman's specialty is [[DNA repair]]. His work with [[Evelyn M. Witkin]] set the basis for the discovery of the [[SOS response]]. The [[SOS response]] hypothesis was put forward by Radman in 1970 in a letter sent to various researchers, and later published in 1974.<ref>{{cite journal | title=Phenomenology of an inducible mutagenic DNA repair pathway in Escherichia coli: SOS repair hypothesis | last=Radman | first=M | journal=In L. Prakash, F. Sherman, M. Miller, C. Lawrence and H. W. Tabor (Ed.), Molecular and Environmental Aspects of Mutagenesis. Charles C Thomas, Springfield, III | year=1974 | volume=6 | pages=128–142}}</ref><ref>{{cite book  | last=Radman | first=M  | title=Molecular Mechanisms for Repair of DNA | chapter=SOS Repair Hypothesis: Phenomenology of an Inducible DNA Repair Which is Accompanied by Mutagenesis | series=Basic Life Sciences | year=1975 | volume=5A | pages=355–367 | pmid=1103845| doi=10.1007/978-1-4684-2895-7_48 | isbn=978-1-4684-2897-1 }}</ref>

With his group he demonstrated the molecular mechanism of speciation by showing that [[DNA mismatch repair]] mechanism prevents [[genetic recombination|recombination]] between similar [[chromosome]]s which leads to establishment of genetic barriers between species.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Rayssiguier C. |author2=Thales DS. |author3=Radman M. | title=The barrier to recombination between Escherichia coli and Salmonella typhimurium is disrupted in mismatch-repair mutants | journal=Nature | year=1989 | volume=342 | issue=6248 | pages=396–401 | doi=10.1038/342396a0| pmid=2555716 | bibcode=1989Natur.342..396R | s2cid=4308035 }}</ref>

In 2011 Radman won the FEMS-[[André Michel Lwoff|Lwoff Award]], given out by the [[FEMS|Federation of European Microbiological Societies]], for his research of DNA repair mechanism in ''[[Deinococcus radiodurans]]''. He clarified the molecular mechanism that allows Deinococcus radiodurans to repair its fatally damaged DNA.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Zahradka K, Slade D, Bailone A, Sommer S, Averbeck D, Petranovic M, Lindner AB, Radman M | title=Reassembly of shattered chromosomes in Deinococcus radiodurans | journal=Nature | volume=443 | issue=7111 | year=2006 | pages=569–573 | url=http://www.insermactualites.net/fileadmin/user_upload/202/fichiers/nature05160Radman.pdf | pmid=17006450 | doi=10.1038/nature05160 | bibcode=2006Natur.443..569Z | s2cid=4412830 }}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="Lwoff award"/>

Radman developed a methodology which enables direct visualization of [[horizontal gene transfer]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Babić A. |author2=Linder AB. |author3=Vulić M. |author4=Stewart AJ |author5=Radman, M. | title=Direct visualization of horizontal gene transfer | journal=Science | year=2008 | volume=319 | issue=5869 | pages=1533–6 | doi=10.1126/science.1153498| pmid=18339941 | bibcode=2008Sci...319.1533B | s2cid=52861268 }}</ref>

==Awards and memberships==
* Antoine Lacassagne Award (1979), Grand Prix of the French League Against Cancer for the discovery of the mutagenic [[SOS response|SOS system]] in bacteria
* Golden Eureka of Innovation (1990)
* [[Grand Prix Charles-Leopold Mayer]] of the French Academy of Science for the co-discovery of [[DNA mismatch repair|DNA error correction (mismatch repair)]]
* Medal of Honour (1992) awarded by Society for the Encouragement of Progress
* Spiridion Brusina Medal (1998) at the 100th anniversary of the Croatian Naturalists' Society
* [[Leopold Griffuel Prize]] for the contributions to the field of [[DNA repair]]
* [[Richard Lounsbery Award]] – Joint Award of the French and U.S. national academies of science for the discovery of [[DNA mismatch repair]] as genetic barrier between related species
* Science Award (2000) from the “U.S. Environmental Mutagen Society” for "far-reaching research contributions to understanding the profound consequences of mutation and recombination, in global genomic responses, DNA repair, cancer and evolution"
* Katzir Katchalsky Honorary Lecturer (2000), [[Weizmann Institute of Science|Weizmann Institute]], [[Israel]]
* [[French Institute of Health and Medical Research|Grand Prix de l'INSERM (2003)]] awarded by the [[French Institute of Health and Medical Research]]
* Leonardo Award (2004) for creativity in scientific research
* FEMS-[[André Michel Lwoff|Lwoff Award]] (2011) for his research of DNA repair mechanism in [[Deinococcus radiodurans]]
* Fellow of [[French Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="BioFR"/>
* Corresponding member of [[Croatian Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name="BioCR"/>
* Foreign honorary member of [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] 
* Member of The Academy of Europe<ref name="AE"/>(2018)
